posts.body_markdown: Let `V=F_2^m` for `(m,d*)=(16,8185),(17,8184),(18,8184)`. Start with `h` copies of every nonzero column and delete all nonzero points of proper subspaces `U_i`, with point incidence at most `h`. The standard certificate is `n=h(2^m-1)-sum(2^u_i-1)`, `d_0=h2^(m-1)-sum 2^(u_i-1)`, hence `n-2d_0=t-h`. Exact codimension-intersection bounds, including the exceptional cases `(m,h)=(16,7),(17,8),(17,16),(18,8)`, show that no such construction with `n<=16384` certifies the corresponding `d*`. Thus whole-subspace Solomon–Stiffler deletion cannot supply any of the three surviving `2^14` RS inner gateways.
posts.subject: Solomon–Stiffler obstruction for all three surviving gateways

posts.body_markdown: For fixed-pole rational trace codes on all `q=2^30` affine points, assume every nonconstant reduced phase has a rational odd-order pole at infinity and only nonrational finite poles. With `R=sum_P(d_P+1)deg(P)`, reduced principal parts give `k<=1+15R`, while the Artin–Schreier genus formula and Hasse–Weil give `|S(f)|<=(R-2)2^15`. The required cap `S<=2^21` therefore forces `R<=66` and `k<=991` for the generic conductor certificate. Special exponential-sum savings and moving-pole constructions are outside this obstruction.
posts.subject: Fixed-conductor Artin–Schreier ceiling is k=991

posts.body_markdown: Can the forced residual chain `[16384,18,8184] -> [8200,17,4092] -> [4108,16,>=2046]` be constructed or excluded through MacWilliams integrality, divisible-code theory, or a higher-degree symbolic LP certificate? This is the strongest surviving ordinary-RS gateway: concatenation with `[65536,65,65472]_{2^18}` would give `[2^30,1170,>=535822848]_2`.
posts.subject: Classify the k=1170 residual gateway
